MAHALAGANG ABISO SA MGA MOTORISTA🚦

Asahan ang pagbagal ng daloy ng trapiko sa kahabaan ng Elliptical Road dahil sa inaasahang pagdagsa ng mga manonood sa Quezon City Countdown to 2026 na gaganapin sa Quezon Memorial Circle sa December 31, 2025 (Wednesday) simula 4:00 PM.

Magtutulungan at nakaantabay ang mga tauhan ng Traffic and Transport Management Department (TTMD), Department of Public Order and Safety (DPOS), Task Force Disiplina, Quezon City Police District (QCPD), at Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) para maisaayos ang inaasahang mabigat na daloy ng trapiko sa nasabing lugar.

Pinapayuhan ang mga motorista na dumaan sa mga alternatibong ruta.

Maraming salamat po sa inyong pang-unawa.

#NewYear2026

Heavy equipment was deployed as crews carried out reblocking of damaged sections and asphalt overlaying across the full width of EDSA from December 24 to 27.

data.raw_text:
A Merry Christmas in a #BagongPilipinas: December 2025 #PBBMGoodNews Highlights

❤️✌️ Thank you for sharing this #PBBMGoodNews

As parols light up the streets and families prepare for Noche Buena, December at Malacañang has been filled with gifts and good vibes.

From holiday blessings to opening the Palace doors to the people, these #PBBMGoodNews moments brought joy, hope, and bayanihan this Christmas season.

🎁 The “Gift of Gratitude”: Bonuses for Workers

Because everyone deserves a joyful Christmas, the biggest gift arrived just in time for the holidays. President Marcos signed Administrative Order No. 40 authorizing the release of the Service Recognition Incentive. Under this order, regular employees in the Executive Branch, SUCs, GOCCs, and uniformed services received a one time cash grant of up to ₱20,000.

Contract of Service and Job Order workers were also included. Through Administrative Order No. 39, they were granted gratuity pay of up to ₱7,000. This was welcome support that helped stretch the holiday budget and add to the Christmas table.

🚗 A Long Weekend to End 2025

To give Filipinos more time to travel home and spend the holidays with family, Malacañang announced a suspension of work in government offices on December 29, Monday, and January 2, Friday. This created a much needed long weekend and made holiday reunions easier and less rushed.

🚆 “12 Days of Christmas” Free Rides

Commuters also received an early Christmas gift with the Department of Transportation’s “12 Days of Libreng Sakay” on MRT 3, LRT 1, and LRT 2. Beginning December 14, free rides were offered daily to different sectors, including students, senior citizens, and OFWs.

Private sector employees and kasambahays enjoyed free rides on December 23. The highlight came on Christmas Day itself. On December 25, all passengers rode for free on MRT and LRT lines, with PNR joining the initiative. This was perfect for holiday trips, family visits, and Christmas errands.

🍲 #WalangGutom This Christmas

The administration’s flagship anti hunger program, #WalangGutom2027, continued to show meaningful progress this December. Based on the latest reports, food insecurity among beneficiary households has dropped to 41.5 percent.

In Pasay City, the Walang Gutom Kitchen, formerly a POGO hub and now transformed into a soup kitchen, became fully operational. It serves free breakfast and lunch every day to street dwellers and families in need. This ensures that no one is left hungry during the holiday season.

🎄 #TaraSaPalasyo: Malacañang Open House (December 16 to 23)

For the fourth year in a row, President Bongbong Marcos opened the gates of Malacañang to the public through the #TaraSaPalasyo Christmas celebrations. Traditional Simbang Gabi, also known as Misa de Gallo, was held at the Palace grounds from December 16 to 24. Free bibingka, puto bumbong, and hot chocolate were served to attendees.

Overseas Filipino Workers were given special attention as well. Recognized by the President as modern day heroes, OFWs were welcomed with a night of carnival rides, gifts, and entertainment. The event was filled with gratitude, celebration, and meaningful bonding.

🛣️ Byaheng #BuildBetterMore

For families traveling north and south this Christmas, infrastructure updates brought good news. The NLEX to SLEX Connector Road and CLLEX Phase 1 are now near completion. These projects significantly reduce travel time, ease traffic congestion, and allow families to spend more precious hours together.

📈 Economy Watch

The year ended on a positive economic note, with inflation remaining within the 2 to 4 percent target range. This helped keep prices more manageable in public markets and allowed families to stretch their holiday budgets and enjoy a more comfortable Christmas celebration.
